subject: Islamic Religious Education

source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Islamic Religious Education, Grade 6 (Revised 2024)
source.notes: Read directly from grade-6-curriculum-desings/GRADE-6-IRE-Curriculum-Designs.pdf via the Read tool (no pages param), full text, all 7 strands / 24 sub-strands / 90 lessons. Learning Area allocation: 3 lessons/week at Upper Primary.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Selected Surah
subStrands.notes: The design names 4 specific surahs under this one sub-strand heading, no further breakdown given: Al-Humaza, Al-Asr, At-Takathur, Al-Qariah. Following the Grade 7 IRE precedent (which split its own single 'Selected Surah' sub-strand into one skill per named surah), this sub-strand is implemented as 4 skills, one per surah — each a short, well-known Meccan surah rich enough in content (themes, closing lessons, vocabulary) to support its own skill.
specificLearningOutcomes: read the selected surahs for use in devotional activities
recite the selected surah for use in ibaadah
explain the basic meaning of the selected surah to enhance positive character formation
discuss the lessons learnt from the selected surah for spiritual nourishment
apply the teachings of the selected surah in their daily life
appreciate the importance of the selected surah by adhering to their teachings
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the effects of backbiting?
How can Muslims use time well?
How can Muslims prepare for the Day of Judgement?
learningExperiences: listen to verses of the selected surah from a teacher/resource person/digital device and repeat afterwards
read and recite the selected surah with the aid of digital devices/mus'haf/chart
discuss the basic meaning of the selected surah and make notes
match and sort the verses of the selected surah with their corresponding meaning using flash cards
brainstorm on the lessons learnt from the selected surah and present in class
dramatise the teachings of the selected surah
linkedLearningAreas: English — learners acquire new vocabularies as they learn the meaning of the surah
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric rewards reading/reciting all four selected surah correctly and coherently, plus explaining basic meaning and lessons with relevant examples — recitation accuracy and applied meaning are both explicitly assessed, not meaning alone.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Hadith on Purity of Actions
specificLearningOutcomes: read the selected Hadith on purity of actions for moral guidance
apply the lessons learnt from the selected Hadith in day-to-day life
uphold the lessons learnt from the Hadith on purity of actions for sincerity in deeds
appreciate purity of actions to gain rewards from Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is appearance and wealth not important in the eyes of Allah?
What does Allah look for when rewarding His servants?
learningExperiences: read the Hadith on purity of action: "Allah does not look at your appearance or wealth, but rather He looks at your heart and actions." (Muslim)
discuss the lessons learnt from the Hadith on purity of actions and make a summary
brainstorm on the relevance of purity of actions in today's society and share the findings on a chart
dramatise situations depicting purity of actions

subStrands.name: 2.2 Hadith on Dressing
specificLearningOutcomes: read the Hadith on Islamic dressing for moral uprightness
describe the male and female dress code as per the Sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.)
practise Islamic manner of dressing as an act of ibadah
embrace the lessons learnt from the Hadith on Islamic dressing
appreciate the Islamic dressing to avoid the wrath of Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should the male and female dress differently?
What is the purpose of dressing?
learningExperiences: read the Hadith on dressing: "The Messenger of Allah (S.A.W.) cursed the man who wears women's clothing and the woman who wears men's clothing." (Abu-Daud)
classify clothes and accessories according to gender (trousers, skirts, blouses, shirts, shorts, necklaces, earrings, bangles, hair dressing) using digital devices/pocket boards/charts
discuss the male and female dress code as per the Sunnah of the Prophet (S.A.W.) and make class presentation
draw and colour different clothes and accessories and display
search for the reasons why the Prophet (S.A.W.) prohibited gender-mixed dressing and write a short essay
model appropriate dress for different gender
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — covers content on dressing for different occasions and decency
scopeNotes: include: PCI flags this sub-strand under Life Skills as 'Human Sexuality aspects realised as learners dress as per Islamic teachings for different genders' — treat with factual, dignified, non-graphic framing (clothing/accessory classification and modesty principle only), matching the same standard already applied to Grade 6 Agriculture's grooming sub-strand.

subStrands.name: 2.3 Hadith on Planting
specificLearningOutcomes: read the Hadith on planting of trees and crops for environmental consciousness
assess the importance of planting trees and crops as an act of ibadah
plant trees and crops for food sustainability to earn rewards from Allah
appreciate the value of planting trees and crops for the benefit of Allah's creatures
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the dangers of cutting down trees?
What are the benefits of growing trees and crops?
learningExperiences: read the Hadith on planting trees and crops: "If a Muslim plants a tree or sows a field and men, animals and birds eat from it, all of it is charity from him." (Muslim)
research on the significance of planting trees and crops and present the findings in class
collect pictures of fruit-bearing plants and crops and display in class
plant trees and crops in the school compound and care for them
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — contains similar content on planting trees and crops

subStrands.name: 2.4 Hadith on Responsible Use of Human Capabilities and Resources
specificLearningOutcomes: read the Hadith on responsible use of human capabilities and resources for character building
assess the significance of using Allah (S.W.T.)'s bounties for the benefit in this life and the Hereafter
use the bounties of Allah (S.W.T.) responsibly in day-to-day life
appreciate the bounties of Allah (S.W.T.) by acting responsibly to get His pleasure
keyInquiryQuestions: What bounties has Allah (S.W.T.) given to mankind?
How should a Muslim use time wisely?
What activities may cause harm to people's health?
How do you spend your pocket money?
learningExperiences: read the Hadith: "Take advantage of five matters before five other matters: your youth before you become old; and your health, before you fall sick; and your wealth, before you become poor; and your free time before you become busy; and your life, before your death." (Ahmad)
discuss the significance of using Allah (S.W.T.)'s bounties and make summary notes
brainstorm on how to use the bounties of Allah (S.W.T.) responsibly and make presentations in class (youthfulness, health, wealth, time, life)
role-play proper usage of Allah (S.W.T.)'s bounties mentioned in the Hadith
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — the concept of time and resource management can be related to Social Studies

subStrands.name: 3.1 Stories of Prophets: Prophet Ibrahim (A.S.) and Prophet Yusuf (A.S.)
subStrands.notes: Design gives a lesson count discrepancy between its own summary table (08) and the detailed sub-strand page (6 Lessons) — treated as one sub-strand either way. Implemented as 2 skills (one per prophet) since each story carries distinct, substantial named episodes: Ibrahim (A.S.) — breaking idols, saved by Allah from the fire, the attempted sacrifice of Ismail; Yusuf (A.S.) — saved from the well, temptation/imprisonment, famine, leadership.
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the stories of the selected prophets to build their faith
explain the lessons learnt from the stories of the prophets for character development
emulate the character of the prophets in day-to-day life
appreciate the selected prophets as role models
keyInquiryQuestions: How did the selected prophets demonstrate Iman in Allah (S.W.T.)?
What virtues are derived from prophets Ibrahim (A.S.) and Musa (A.S.)'s stories?
learningExperiences: listen/watch the stories of the selected prophets (Ibrahim (A.S.) breaking idols, saved by Allah (S.W.T.) from fire and attempt to sacrifice Ismail; Prophet Yusuf (A.S.) — Allah (S.W.T.) saved him from the well, temptation/imprisonment, famine and leadership) using digital devices
brainstorm on how the selected prophets demonstrated their steadfastness in faith in Allah (S.W.T.)
deduce lessons from the stories of the selected prophets and make short notes
discuss relevance of the stories of the selected prophets and present on a chart
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — has some aspects of values an individual should have which are the same as those of the prophets in Islam

subStrands.name: 3.2 Taqwa (God Consciousness)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the qualities of a pious person (Muttaqiin) for character building
assess the significance of taqwa in the life of a Muslim
demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.) as a mark of true belief
appreciate the virtue of taqwa as a pre-condition for success in this life and the Hereafter
keyInquiryQuestions: What actions lead to piety?
Why is taqwa important in the life of a Muslim?
learningExperiences: read verses (Q. 2:2-5, 3:133-135) from the Qur'an/digital devices/mus'haf and list down the qualities of mutaqiin
match and sort the qualities of a pious person using flash cards
search online/from a mus'haf verse (Q.2:43, 76, 7:96, 9:119, 19:72) on taqwa and draw their significance
keep a weekly log/diary on the activities that demonstrate taqwa
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — has some aspect of integrity which is related to God consciousness

subStrands.name: 3.3 Tawakkul (Reliance on Allah)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the qualities of a mutawakkil as a basis for character building
assess the significance of tawakkul in the life of a Muslim
practise tawakkul in day-to-day life
appreciate the virtue of tawakkul as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter
keyInquiryQuestions: How can a Muslim show reliance on Allah?
Why is tawakkul important to a Muslim?
learningExperiences: brainstorm and identify the qualities of a mutawakkil and display them on the notice board (Q.3:160, Q5:23, Q65:3)
sort the qualities of a mutawakkil using a digital device/pocket board/flash cards
discuss the significance of tawakkul in the life of a Muslim and make summary notes
discuss ways in which Muslims can practise tawakkul in their daily life
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — has some aspect of integrity which is related to reliance on God

subStrands.name: 4.1 Twahara (Purity): Hadath, Optional Ghusl
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the types of Hadath for ritual purity (Twahara)
differentiate between Hadath Asghar and Hadath Akbar to promote personal hygiene
explain the reasons for performance of tayyamum as a pre-condition for swalah
identify situations for the performance of sunnah ghusl
demonstrate ways of purification of Hadath Asghar and Hadath Akbar to maintain ritual purity
appreciate maintenance of ritual purity as a condition for Ibadah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should Muslims maintain ritual purity?
learningExperiences: identify the types of Hadath
discuss the difference between Hadath Asghar and Hadath Akbar and present in tabular form
identify items to be used in the purification of Hadath Asghar and Hadath Akbar and present on a chart
sort and match the types of Hadath and methods of purification (wudhu, tayyamum, ghusl) using digital devices/flashcards/pocket boards/charts
discuss situations when tayyamum is performed
brainstorm on situations when optional ghusl is performed and make summary notes
demonstrate the steps of performing tayamum
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — personal hygiene is covered in this learning area

subStrands.name: 4.2 Zakat
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the items liable for zakaat payment for spiritual growth
describe the eight recipients of zakat as mentioned in the Qur'an
differentiate between zakaat and sadaqa to inculcate the spirit of giving
appreciate the need to pay zakat and sadaqa to develop empathy
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim pay zakaat?
learningExperiences: collect pictures of items/commodities liable for zakaat and display/mount on charts
use digital devices/Qur'an to search for the recipients of zakaat and make notes (Q9:60)
use flash cards/pocket boards/charts to show the difference between zakat and sadaqa
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics — the concept of payment of zakaat involves some calculations of nisab and rate which can be related
subStrands.assessmentSignal: Rubric distinguishes 'identifies items + all 8 recipients with Hadith evidence' from 'identifies items + only 4-6 recipients' from 'less than 4 recipients' — the full 8 recipients (Q9:60) is an explicit, graded target, not a rough sample.

subStrands.name: 4.3 Saum (Fasting)
specificLearningOutcomes: state the categories of people who are exempted from obligatory fast
explain the reasons for fidya (compensation) by people exempted from fasting during the month of Ramadhan
describe different ways of compensating for missed fasts
appreciate Allah (S.W.T.)'s mercy to Muslims for exemption of fasting with valid reasons
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are some people exempted from fasting?
learningExperiences: identify the categories of people exempted from fasting as mentioned in the Qur'an and list them in their note books (Q2:184-185)
use digital devices/flash cards to search and match the categories of people exempted from fasting with the corresponding ways of compensation
discuss different ways of compensating for missed fasts and make notes
discuss the reasons why Allah (S.W.T.) exempted some people from fasting and make presentations
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — in aspects of intermittent fasting

subStrands.name: 4.4 Hajj
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the conditions of Hajj for validity of its performance
explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each
describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity
appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the prerequisites for the performance of Hajj?
What is the significance of Hajj?
learningExperiences: search for the conditions of Hajj and make notes
discuss the different types of Hajj and present on a chart
search and watch video clips on the performance of Hajj
search for verses on Hajj from the Qur'an and Hadith and display on charts
create a model Kaaba and simulate the performance of Hajj
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — has aspects of visiting religious places/shrines as part of social organisation of different communities

subStrands.name: 5.1 Virtues: Work as a form of Ibadah
specificLearningOutcomes: state the reasons why work is considered as Ibadah in Islam
explain the benefits of work in the development of the Ummah
describe different types of work as means to lawful earnings
differentiate between halal and haram work
appreciate the importance of work as a form of Ibadah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim work?
Why is work considered an act of Ibadah?
What kind of work is prohibited in Islam?
learningExperiences: discuss why work is considered Ibadah in Islam
brainstorm on the benefits of work and present in class
collect pictures of different occupations and display them in class
search and watch video clips on different types of work and differentiate between permissible and non-permissible
identify ethics that should guide work in Islam
dramatise different types of works as means of earning a living
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — learners are taught different types of work/professions

subStrands.name: 5.1 Virtues: Adalah (Justice)
subStrands.notes: Source PDF numbers this sub-strand '5.1' a second time (a duplicate heading, not a typo we should silently renumber) — its own summary table lists it separately as '5.2 Adalah, Justice'. Kept as its own distinct sub-strand/skill.
specificLearningOutcomes: assess the importance of adalah as a means of promoting fairness in the society
describe different instances where justice must be practised to ensure fairness in the society
practise justice and fairness in day-to-day life
appreciate the virtue of adalah as a way of earning rewards from Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the benefits of observing adalah in the society?
How can a pupil practise adalah in school?
learningExperiences: discuss the importance of exercising justice and make class presentation
search for verses in the Qur'an that advocate for fairness (Q. 4:135)
read a story on justice and draw lessons on fairness
role-play actions that depict justice
make and present short skits thematising adalah in society
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — covers aspects of human rights and justice

subStrands.name: 5.2 Prohibitions in Islam: Intoxicants
subStrands.notes: PDF's own summary table lists this as '5.3 Prohibitions in Islam, Intoxicants'.
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the types of intoxicants rampant in the society
explain the effects of intoxicants on the society
describe ways of curbing the use of intoxicants
adhere to Islamic teachings on prohibition of intoxicants in day-to-day life
appreciate the prohibition of intoxicants for the wellbeing of the society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why does Islam prohibit the use of intoxicants?
What are the effects of intoxicants on the society?
learningExperiences: discuss and list intoxicants rampant in the community
research on the negative effects of intoxicants and make short notes
search and watch age-appropriate videos on the effects of intoxicants
make posters on the effects of intoxicants
story-tell/dramatise effects of intoxicants
brainstorm on ways of curbing the use of intoxicants and make posters
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology — content on the effects of intoxicants (drug and substance abuse) is covered

subStrands.name: 5.2 Prohibitions in Islam: Israf (Extravagance)
subStrands.notes: PDF's own summary table lists this as '5.4 Israf, extravagance'.
specificLearningOutcomes: identify resources available in the community
explain ways of guarding against israf for effective resource management
explain the effects of israf in the society
use available resources effectively as a way of promoting economic growth
appreciate proper use of resources to get rewards from Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to avoid israf?
How can people promote good use of resources?
learningExperiences: discuss resources that are often wasted e.g. food, water, money and present

dramatise appropriate ways of using resources in accordance with Islamic teachings (e.g. serve food enough for self; not using excessive amounts of water while performing wudhu; turning off TV/lights when not in use)
make posters/signage discouraging israf and pin them at strategic places e.g. turn off taps when not in use
brainstorm on the effects of israf and make presentations
linkedLearningAreas: Agriculture — wastage of resources is covered

subStrands.name: 5.3 Dua (Supplication when Travelling)
subStrands.notes: PDF's own summary table lists this as '5.5 Dua (supplication when traveling)'.
specificLearningOutcomes: recite the dua for travelling to seek Allah (S.W.T.)'s protection
recite the dua in day-to-day life while travelling
appreciate the importance of the dua for travelling in seeking protection from Allah (S.W.T.)
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to recite a dua while travelling?
What safety precautions should one observe while travelling?
learningExperiences: read the dua: "Glory to Him who has brought this (e.g. vehicle) under our control, though we were unable to control it (ourselves), and indeed, to our Lord we will surely return." (Muslim)
note the dua in the books and memorise
role-play travelling and recite the dua in class
discuss safe practices a passenger should observe while in a vehicle (such as boarding through door, be seated when the vehicle is in motion and avoid distracting the driver)
discuss the importance of reciting the dua when travelling and make notes and class presentation
write the dua on charts and post them on the school's notice board

subStrands.name: 6.1 Fair Treatment of Workers
specificLearningOutcomes: state the rights of workers to promote a conducive working environment
describe ways of treating workers fairly
practise Islamic ethics while relating with workers
appreciate Islamic teachings on workers by treating them fairly
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should workers be treated well?
How can we treat workers fairly?
learningExperiences: discuss the rights of workers and make notes
discuss appropriate ways of treating workers and present on charts
role-play fair treatment of workers
share personal experiences on how workers are treated in homes
brainstorm on ways of promoting fair treatment of workers

discuss the Hadith of the Prophet (S.A.W.) on fair treatment of workers: "Your brothers are your responsibility. Allah has made them under your hands. So, whosoever has a brother under his hand, let him give him food as he eats and dress as he dresses. Do not give them work that will overburden them and if you give them such tasks, then provide assistance." (Bukhari)
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — human rights concepts are covered in the subject

subStrands.name: 6.2 Relations with People of Other Faiths
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the rights of non-Muslims for harmonious living
describe ways of promoting good relations with people of other faiths for peaceful co-existence
demonstrate ways of living harmoniously with people of other faiths in day-to-day life
appreciate living with people of other faiths harmoniously
keyInquiryQuestions: How should Muslims relate with people of other faiths?
What are the rights of the people of other faiths?
learningExperiences: research on the rights of non-Muslims from available reference materials and make class presentation
discuss ways of living peacefully with non-Muslims and display on a chart (Q. 2:256, 8:61, 60:8, 109:6)
role-play ways of living harmoniously with people of other faiths
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — has some aspects of harmonious living

subStrands.name: 6.3 Corruption
specificLearningOutcomes: identify forms of corruption to create awareness in the society
explain the effects of corruption to inculcate the value of integrity
describe ways of curbing corruption for fairness and accountability
promote a corruption-free society by observing Islamic ethics and taqwa
appreciate the teachings of Islam against corruption by upholding Islamic morals
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is corruption prohibited in Islam?
What can you do to stop corruption?
What are the effects of corruption in our society?
learningExperiences: discuss forms of corruption in their environment (such as exam cheating, inflating bus fare, withholding shopping balance, election, deceiving parents on school levies) and make brief presentation
search for Hadiths/Qur'anic verses on corruption and write the teachings (Q. 2:11-12, 27, 30, 188)
brainstorm on the effects of corruption and display on charts
design posters on ways of curbing corruption
role-play acts depicting forms of corruption and ways of eradicating them
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — content on corruption is covered

subStrands.name: 7.1 The Battles of Badr and Uhud
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the reasons that led to the battles of Badr and Uhud to appreciate Islamic heritage
narrate the events of the battles of Badr and Uhud for spiritual nourishment
explain the effects of the battles of Badr and Uhud to strengthen their Iman
appreciate reliance on Allah (S.W.T.) in overcoming challenges in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: What lessons can Muslims learn from the battles of Badr and Uhud?
learningExperiences: search for the reasons that led to the battles of Badr and Uhud and make notes

watch video clips/listen to narrations on the battles of Badr and Uhud and draw lessons (such as praying to Allah (S.W.T.) for help in times of difficulties, true victory comes from Allah (S.W.T.) (Q. 3:123-128), the importance of knowledge, fair treatment of captives)
brainstorm on the effects of the battles of Badr and Uhud and make class presentations
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — learners study the content on the effects of conflicts and conflict resolution

subStrands.name: 7.2 The Treaty of Hudaibiya
specificLearningOutcomes: state the terms of the treaty of Hudaibiya as part of Islamic History
adopt peaceful conflict resolution methods in day-to-day life
appreciate the treaty of Hudaibiya as a guide to peaceful coexistence
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to resolve conflicts through peaceful means?
How can Muslims apply the lessons learnt from the treaty of Hudaibiya?
learningExperiences: search from reference materials on the treaty of Hudaibiya and write the terms of the treaty
dramatise acts depicting peaceful ways of resolving conflicts, drawing lessons from what they have learnt from the treaty of Hudaibiya
make posters on the terms of the treaty of Hudaibiya
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — conflict resolution mechanisms are covered

subStrands.name: 7.3 The Conquest of Makkah (Fat-hul Makkah), including the Battle of Hunayn
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the events that led to the conquest of Makkah for spiritual nourishment
deduce lessons from the conquest of Makkah for peaceful co-existence
state the reasons that led to the battle of Hunayn
explain the effects of the battle of Hunayn to strengthen their Iman
apply the lessons from the conquest of Makkah in day-to-day life
appreciate clemency as part of the Sunnah of the prophet (S.A.W.)
keyInquiryQuestions: What lessons do Muslims learn from the events of fat-hul Makkah?
Why should one forgive people who have wronged them?
learningExperiences: listen to a story/watch a video/film on fat-hul Makkah and make a presentation on the events
discuss the lessons learnt from the events of fat-hul Makkah and display on charts (e.g. forgiveness, purity of places of worship, love of one's enemies as an effective daawa, Islam stands for peace)
discuss the reasons that led to the battle of Hunayn and make class presentation
discuss the effects of the battle of Hunayn and write notes
dramatise acts depicting peaceful ways of resolving conflicts from the events of fat-hul Makkah
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — conflict resolution mechanisms are covered

subStrands.name: 7.4 Farewell Pilgrimage (Hijjatul Wid'a): Farewell Sermon
specificLearningOutcomes: state the teachings contained in Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)'s farewell sermon for spiritual nourishment
deduce lessons from Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)'s farewell sermon as a basis for character formation
apply the lessons learnt from the prophet (S.A.W.)'s farewell sermon in day-to-day life
appreciate the Prophet (S.A.W.)'s farewell speech as a guide to mankind
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the main themes in Hijjatul Wid'a?
How can Muslims apply the lessons from the farewell sermon in today's world?
learningExperiences: read the farewell sermon, deduce the teachings and make presentations in class
identify key themes from the speech and make notes

brainstorm on the lessons learnt from Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.)'s farewell sermon and make notes (such as sanctity of life and property, equality of human beings, Muslim brotherhood, not hurting one another, observing the pillars of Islam)
role-play acts depicting the teachings of the Prophet (S.A.W.)'s farewell sermon
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies — aspects of human rights mentioned during the farewell address are covered in these subjects

implementationNotes: 24 raw sub-strands, split into 28 skills where the design names 2+ genuinely distinct named items within one sub-strand heading (4 surahs under 1.1; 2 prophets under 3.1), following the exact precedent set by Grade 7 IRE's own surah-splitting and this project's Grade 6-wide 'split into more, smaller, deeper skills' policy. Strand ids in curriculum.ts: g6-ire-quran (QU.1-4), g6-ire-hadith (HA.1-4), g6-ire-iman (PI.1-4), g6-ire-devotional (DA.1-4), g6-ire-akhlaq (AK.1-5), g6-ire-muamalat (MU.1-3), g6-ire-history (HI.1-4).
